subject: Materials Science
title: Basalt Fiber: Volcanic Reinforcement
description: A short lesson to help you apply Basalt Fiber: Volcanic Reinforcement.

hook.text: Melt volcanic basalt rock at 1,500°C, pull it into threads, and you get a green-friendly fiber.

buildup.text: Basalt fiber is stronger and stiffer than E-glass, with better chemical and heat resistance.

discovery.text: It needs no additives — just crushed basalt rock melted and drawn, a simpler process than glass fiber.

twist.text: Basalt fiber costs more than glass but less than carbon — a middle-ground many industries want.

climax.text: Bridge reinforcement, fire-resistant panels, and offshore pipes are adopting basalt fiber fast.

punchline.text: Lava rock, melted and spun, becomes tomorrow's composite fiber.

quiz.question: What is basalt fiber made from?
